data.title: 'Non-answers' aren't working. This is what investors really need from the Fed.
data.description:
By Greg Robb

Chair Kevin Warsh has to make a U-turn in communication

Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh speaks during his news conference in September.

The headline coming out of the Federal Reserve's meeting Wednesday will be the central bank's decision on interest rates, but what really matters to investors, economists say, is for Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh to prove he can successfully communicate the central bank's strategy.

Analysts want to know whether the hot inflation readings for September were a game-changing development, and what criteria the Fed will use to assess the timing and pace of subsequent rate hikes. They'll be watching Warsh's press conference Wednesday for signs that the central bank has a strategy for curbing prices after more than five years of inflation above its 2% target.

"The market cares about the final destination," more than the outcome of Wednesday's meeting, said Juhi Dhawan, global macroanalyst at Wellington Management.

Right now, the market expects a "shallow" Fed tightening of up to three rate hikes by the end of the first quarter of 2027. There have been many periods when the Fed has tightened only a few times, she said. That strategy fits with the narrative that the Fed is reversing the three cuts the central bank made last year over concern about the labor market.

There's a possibility they could take a more aggressive approach with a full rate hike. A "full" rate-hiking cycle would be 150 or 200 basis points, Dhawan said, which would take rates back up to the highest levels since 2023.

Derek Tang, co-founder of forecasting firm LH Meyer, said the market has a very difficult time understanding when the rate hikes will end.

"Do the hikes end when inflation literally is at 2%?" Tang asked.

Previous Fed chairs have provided a forecast, such as saying something like: The Fed can hike until underlying inflation gets low enough and then the central bank will hold rates steady. But Warsh hasn't provided any signals about the Fed's approach.

"It is a little bit of a black box," Tang said. "He's become quite skilled at giving non-answers."

The ultimate level of rates will impact borrowers and homebuyers. If rates go high enough, it could even choke off the current economic expansion.

A less-is-more approach

When Warsh came into office in May, he installed a sea change in Fed communication that can best be summed up as "less is more." A quieter Fed would let the market speak louder, he said.

This approach has proven to be a mistake, said Nicholas Economides, a professor of economics at the Stern School of Business at New York University.

"The new Fed chair has missed his chance to define policy coherently by proposing to 'listen to the market,' when the market in fact wants to listen to him," Economides said in an interview.

Warsh's silence on his views on the path forward for interest rates essentially gives away the Fed's authority to the market, he added.

"Unless the Fed speaks authoritatively, over and above what market considerations are, it will just lose its voice," Economides said.

He pointed to market moves after the Fed's September rate hike as an example.

At his September press conference, Warsh declined to answer whether he thought the first hike in three years would be a one-off event or the start of a series of hikes.

Without any guidance, markets pushed interest rates on longer-term Treasurys significantly higher, with the 10-year yield rising to 5.3%, as the market priced in an aggressive Fed with a rate hike in October.

-Greg Robb

data.title: China's Communist Party names new provincial chiefs ahead of fifth plenum
data.description:
By Eduardo Baptista

China's ruling Communist Party announced key personnel changes in six provinces on Saturday, two days before it holds a closed-door conclave in Beijing from October 26 to 29.

The official focus of the secretive meeting, also known as a plenum, in the Chinese capital is expected to be party governance and discipline, though personnel issues could also feature.

Here are the appointments:

  • State Council Vice Secretary-General Wang Zhijun was named Communist Party secretary of the southern province of Hunan, replacing Shen Xiaoming

  • Wang is a full member of the Central Committee, the ​largest of the party's top decision-making bodies

  • Mo Gaoyi, a vice minister at the party's publicity department and director of the State Council Information Office, was named party secretary of the southwestern province of Yunnan, replacing Wang Ning

  • Xie Weijiang, Hunan's deputy party secretary and party chief of Yueyang, a city in the province's northeast, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Mao Weiming

  • Guo Ningning, Fujian's deputy party secretary and party chief of the provincial capital Fuzhou, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling she is set to become governor

  • Lin Tao was named Fujian deputy party secretary, while Qin Haixiang replaced Guo as Fuzhou party chief

  • Zhuge Yujie, previously deputy party secretary of central Hubei province, was named deputy party secretary of the northwestern province of Qinghai and secretary of its provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to become governor

  • Chen Yongqi, southern Jiangxi's deputy party secretary and head of its political and legal affairs commission, was named secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to replace former governor Ye Jianchun, who was placed under investigation in August

  • Zhao Chenxin was named deputy party secretary of the northern province of Hebei and secretary of the provincial government's party group, signalling he is set to succeed Governor Wang Zhengpu

  • Provincial legislatures must formally elect the gubernatorial appointments, but that is generally a procedural step after the party's decision

XTZ Info

Tezos is a distinctive blockchain platform architected to facilitate and govern decentralized applications (dApps) and smart contracts. Its foundation is built on a decentralized governance system that enables blockchain modifications through a community-led decision-making process.

Operating on a unique iteration of Proof of Stake (PoS) mechanism known as Liquid Proof of Stake (LPoS), Tezos allows participants owning more than 6,000 Tez (XTZ) to become delegates, or “bakers”. These bakers are responsible for creating, signing, and publishing new blocks on the Tezos blockchain, and endorsing blocks produced by other bakers. Furthermore, the network utilizes the Michelson programming language for the creation of smart contracts, which engage with the network’s cryptocurrency, Tez, for transaction execution and gas payment.

The native token of Tezos, XTZ, or Tez, plays a multifaceted role within the ecosystem. It serves as a reward for participation in the creation and endorsement of new blocks, either directly or through delegation. It functions as a voting mechanism within the decentralized governance system. Additionally, it is a means of value transfer and is used to pay for gas, the unit of computational effort in Tezos, necessary for executing transactions and interacting with smart contracts.

data.title: The 10-Point: The Ultrawealthy Turn to Kids' Investment Accounts in a Bid for Goodwill — WSJ Newsletter
data.description:
Emma Tucker

1. FROM MY DESK

The world's richest people are embracing a new form of philanthropy: giving a couple hundred dollars to children, one investment account at a time.

Elon Musk is pledging (SpaceX) shares to millions of kids, joining Michael Dell and other billionaires in seeding the new Trump Accounts program. The effort comes as Silicon Valley titans are increasingly cast as societal villains. Communities across the country are opposing data centers, and some polling shows many Americans say they want billionaires to have less political, economic and cultural power.

The payouts idea came from tech investor Brad Gerstner, who sold the concept to the White House and envisions it as a new social contract between the wealthiest Americans and the rest of society. Critics see a political stunt packed with tax advantages for the ultrarich. Erich Schwartzel and Konrad Putzier explore whether these giveaways can keep the pitchforks at bay.

This is an edition of The 10-Point newsletter, a guided tour of the best coverage in The Wall Street Journal. If you're not subscribed, sign up here. If you're reading this in your inbox, tap the headline above for online and audio versions of this newsletter.

2. TODAY'S HEADLINES

  • House Democrats are targeting Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, weighing impeachment as one of their first moves if they take back the House in the midterms.
  • A wave of AI-powered attacks has hit the internet in recent weeks, as hackers armed with agents and other tools make intrusions faster and far harder to trace.
  • The yellow-vest protest movement paralyzed Paris eight years ago. Now it is re-emerging as part of a coalition across France demanding solutions to the high cost of living and other economic complaints.
  • Ukraine said its Starlink system was working normally again, raising hopes of an end to the dayslong disruption to the vital satellite internet service by Elon Musk's SpaceX was ending.
  • An Anduril-backed startup is genetically engineering military dogs to run faster, have a keener sense of smell and avoid inherited diseases.
  • Our national security correspondent got rare access to a U.S. aircraft carrier conducting missions in the Strait of Hormuz, as it prepares for potential strikes on Iranian targets.

3. FROM THE MARKETS

  • To the scientific world, Moderna's cancer vaccine's results proved that a highly personalized, immune-targeting medication can work. To investors, it didn't work well enough, with shares tanking. Columnist David Wainer writes that even after the sharp fall, the drugmaker's stock assumes wild successes.

4. READ IT HERE FIRST

Government grift emerges as a defining midterm issue.

Less than two weeks before the midterms, corruption is suddenly eclipsing inflation as voters' top concern. A string of damaging headlines about the president's inner circle-ranging from a longtime adviser facing a Justice Department inquiry, to a Russian businessman funding his son's lavish wedding afterparty-has left Republican operatives wringing their hands. With Democrats hammering the issue in ads, strategists worry these self-dealing allegations could make a challenging election even harder. Our reporters break down the growing anxiety, and why the fallout could cost Republicans at the ballot box.

5.

The secret playbook behind A24's Elizabeth Holmes smash hit.

For nearly three years, indie studio A24 pulled off a minor Hollywood miracle: keeping its Elizabeth Holmes documentary a complete secret-even from most of its employees. Fewer than 10 staffers knew directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim had embedded with the convicted Theranos fraudster just weeks before she reported to federal prison. That secrecy eventually became the film's most potent marketing weapon. "You Can See Everything" scored a $15 million box-office debut-the biggest for a non-music documentary since 2004. John Jurgensen and Ben Fritz reveal how the studio turned a stealth production into a massive cultural phenomenon.

Get more of the journalism you love. Choose the Journal as a preferred source on Google.

6. SEE THE STORY

You were once smarter than AI at math. Yes, even you.

Five years ago, frontier AI models could barely pass a basic arithmetic test. Today, those same systems have graduated from grade-school homework to solving open research problems that eluded humans for decades. Columnist Ben Cohen looks at how AI went from failing simple math to transforming the field forever. Can you beat the early AI models? Take the quiz.

7. HAPPENING THIS WEEKEND

  • Saturday: Protests are planned across France, with yellow-vest demonstrators, students and labor unions expected to participate. The Tampa Bay Rays face the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 2 of the World Series.
  • Sunday: Brazil holds a closely contested presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. The NFL stages its first regular-season game in Paris, despite the protests.
  • Today's paper

8. THE NUMBER

57

That is the median age for becoming a grandmother today, up from 44 in 1960. Because Americans are waiting longer to have children, this demographic shift is shrinking the healthy years grandparents get to spend actively involved with their grandkids from 28 years down to just 15. But there is a silver lining: Older, retired people are more likely to have time to be with grandchildren, and spending on each grandchild grows as family sizes shrink.

9. AND FINALLY...

The biggest No. 1 in Billboard history is one you might not have heard.

Ella Langley's country hit "Choosin' Texas" recently broke a Billboard Hot 100 record by spending 24 weeks in the top spot, dethroning Mariah Carey. With attention split across a million platforms and highly personalized TikTok algorithms, old mainstream unifiers like radio and TV have lost much of their power. And because the hit didn't top the streaming charts in markets like New York and Los Angeles, it shows how a massive multiweek No. 1 can easily pass people by when media is no longer centralized.

data.title: Wingify Appoints Sahil Sharma As Global Chief People Officer
data.description:
Sharma joins Wingify after a decade at RateGain, where he held senior HR roles spanning people strategy, organisational development and talent management

Wingify has appointed Sahil Sharma as its global chief people officer, effective October 2026. He joins the software company after a decade at RateGain, where he held several senior human resources leadership positions, most recently serving as group chief human resources officer and chair of RGForALL.

Sharma brings experience across people strategy, organisational development, performance management, talent acquisition, employer branding and learning. His career spans technology, business-to-business software-as-a-service (SaaS), digital media and healthcare services.

Leadership Role At RateGain

Sharma served as group chief human resources officer and chair of RGForALL at RateGain from October 2022 to October 2026. He joined the company in 2016 as senior manager for global learning and organisational effectiveness before taking on broader responsibilities, including the role of associate vice-president of human resources.

During his tenure, he worked across people and culture leadership, HR transformation, cross-border mergers and acquisitions, and initial public offering (IPO) journeys.

Earlier Career In HR

Before joining RateGain, Sharma spent four years at IndiaMART InterMESH in strategic HR and learning roles. From July 2012 to May 2015, he served as manager of learning and capacity development, overseeing learning initiatives across India. He later became senior manager of strategic human resources within the HR Centre of Excellence.

Sharma began his career at Serco in 2009, working in training roles supporting a US healthcare client. He served as a process trainer before becoming team leader for training.

Focus On People Strategy

Beyond human resources, Sharma has led sales enablement and customer experience initiatives, bringing a business-oriented perspective to people strategy. He has also advocated the use of artificial intelligence to improve HR processes and business performance.

At Wingify, he will lead the company's global people function, drawing on his experience in talent development, organisational effectiveness and aligning HR priorities with business objectives.

Academic And Advisory Roles

Sharma holds qualifications in business administration and management from Cornell University and in human resource management from the Indian Institute of Management Calcutta.

He is also a member of the Board of Advisors at Chandigarh University, a position he took up in June 2026.

data.title: Whirlpool India Names Abhish Jain CFO Of Elica India
data.description:
The finance director takes over from Nishant Hundiwala as the subsidiary reshuffles its senior leadership from 1 April 2027

Whirlpool of India has appointed Abhish Jain as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of its material subsidiary, Elica India, effective 1 April 2027. Jain, who currently serves as Director – Finance at Whirlpool of India, will succeed Nishant Hundiwala, whose resignation takes effect on 31 March 2027. The change forms part of a wider leadership transition at Elica India, with Anish Ahuja set to take over as managing director from the same date.

The appointments were disclosed under Regulation 30 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements Regulations, 2015.

CFO Transition At Elica India

Hundiwala has resigned from his position as CFO, citing personal reasons, according to the company’s disclosure. His tenure will conclude on 31 March 2027, with Jain assuming the role the following day.

Jain’s appointment brings a finance executive from the parent company into the subsidiary’s top finance position. He will report to Ahuja, who is currently serving as Elica India’s chief operating officer and will become managing director on 1 April 2027.

Finance Experience Across Functions

Jain is a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI). His experience spans commercial finance, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), and manufacturing finance, including roles in India and international markets.

His move to Elica India follows his tenure as Director – Finance at Whirlpool of India. The company disclosure does not specify further details of his previous positions or the priorities he will pursue as CFO.

Wider Leadership Changes

The finance transition coincides with the conclusion of Pralhad Bhutada’s employment agreement as managing director and chief executive officer of Elica India on 31 March 2027. His role and board membership will end on that date.

Ahuja, who became chief operating officer on 1 September 2026, will succeed Bhutada as managing director from 1 April 2027 and report to Elica India’s board chairman.

Ahuja has more than 32 years of experience, including over 26 years with Whirlpool of India, across sales, customer service and supply chain management. Before becoming Elica India’s COO, he served as vice-president of service at Whirlpool of India, overseeing the service profit and loss function.

The appointments mark an internal leadership transition, with Jain moving from the parent company’s finance leadership to the subsidiary as Elica India prepares for a change in its top executive role.

data.title: NANOBIOTIX Announces Final Data from Phase 1 Study Evaluating JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) With Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors as a 2L+ Therapy in Anti-PD-1-Resistant Primary Cutaneous Melanoma
data.description:
Key points:
  • In 24 heavily pre-treated patients with advanced primary cutaneous melanoma whose cancer had progressed after multiple prior lines of therapy including anti-PD-1 therapy, data continue to show an acceptable safety profile and early signals of efficacy
  • 41.7% (10/24) overall response rate (ORR) per RECIST 1.1, including 4 complete responses
  • 75% (18/24) disease control rate (DCR)
  • 17.8 months median Overall Survival
  • Exploratory analysis in a subset of patients (n=8) identified IL-1β, a cytokine linked to treatment-induced anti-tumor immunity, as the most increased plasma cytokine after treatment
  • Investigators concluded that these preliminary findings warrant further evaluation in randomized clinical trials for patients with primary cutaneous melanoma naïve or refractory to anti-PD-1

Data presented at the 2026 Congress of the European Society for Medical Oncology

PARIS and CAMBRIDGE, Mass., Oct. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- NANOBIOTIX (Euronext: NANO - NASDAQ: NBTX - the “Company”), a late-stage clinical biotechnology company pioneering physics-based approaches to expand treatment possibilities for patients with cancer and other major diseases, today announced updated results from patients with anti-PD-1-resistant advanced primary cutaneous melanoma treated in the ongoing Phase 1 Study 1100. The study evaluates JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3), which works in the presence of radiotherapy, followed by an immune checkpoint inhibitor (nivolumab or pembrolizumab) in patients with advanced solid tumors. The data were presented by Jason Chan, MD, Associate Professor, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center, in a poster session on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at the 2026 Annual Meeting of the European Society for Medical Oncology (“ESMO”) in Madrid, Spain.

ABSTRACT #3956: Safety and Anti-Tumor Activity of NBTXR3/SBRT with Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Anti-PD-1 Resistant Melanoma: Results from a Phase I Dose Expansion

J. Chan, J. Lee, A. Lam, A. Daud, F. Collichio, H. Yu, P. Mody, J. Weiss, S. Moschos, S. Powell, S. Peck, M. Lohr, E. Redstone, Z. Li, W. Smith, A. Juloori, R. Gineste, D. Rolando, A. Rosenberg and C. Shen. UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center; UNC Lineberger Comprehensive Cancer Center, The University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill; Sanford Cancer Center; St Luke's University Hospital; The University of Chicago; Nanobiotix

Patients with advanced anti-PD-1 resistant primary cutaneous melanoma whose disease has progressed after multiple prior lines of therapy have a poor prognosis; published series report a median progression-free survival of approximately three months1 and a median overall survival of approximately one year2 in this setting. Melanoma has historically been considered radioresistant, and higher radiation doses are often limited by exposure of the surrounding healthy tissue.

“Patients whose melanoma has progressed on anti-PD-1 therapy, and often on several other immunotherapies as well, have limited options left,” said Jason Chan, MD, Associate Professor, Department of Radiation Oncology, UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center “In this study, a single injection followed by a short course of stereotactic radiotherapy was feasible across a wide range of tumor sizes and locations, and we saw responses in lesions that were injected and in lesions that were not. The observed increase in IL-1β suggests treatment-related immune activation that warrants further investigation. These are early data from a single-arm study, and they support testing the approach in a randomized trial.”

All 24 heavily pre-treated patients had advanced primary cutaneous melanoma resistant to anti-PD-1; 14 had stage IV disease. Most had received other immunotherapies before enrolling, including anti-CTLA-4 (50%), anti-LAG-3 (33.3%) and T-VEC (25%), and 87.5% had received immunotherapy as their most recent therapy. Patients received a one-time intratumoral injection of JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) at the recommended Phase 2 dose (33% of gross tumor volume), followed by stereotactic body radiotherapy (“SBRT”) to the injected lesion and then nivolumab or pembrolizumab. Investigators observed an acceptable safety profile and early signals of efficacy.

Safety and Feasibility

Treatment consisting of a single intratumoral JNJ-1900 (NBTXR3) injection, followed by a short course of radiotherapy was feasible across a wide range of melanoma lesions, providing a minimally invasive treatment approach with an acceptable safety profile. No new safety signals have been observed.

Preliminary Efficacy

An Overall Response Rate (ORR) of 41.7% (10/24 patients) was observed. Responses were observed in both injected (ORR 45.8%; 11/24 evaluable patients) and non-injected lesions (ORR 30.0%; 3/10 evaluable patients).

Median Progression Free Survival (PFS) was 6.9 months, while median Overall Survival reached 17.8 months.

Exploratory Immune Profiling

In an exploratory analysis of plasma samples from a subset of patients (n=8), IL-1β showed the largest increase from baseline among the cytokines evaluated. Media Release

COPENHAGEN, Denmark and WILMINGTON, Del.; October 24, 2026

  • Phase 1/2 study will evaluate petosemtamab plus INCB161734 and standard-of-care chemotherapy in first-line KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC)

Genmab A/S (Nasdaq: GMAB) and Incyte (Nasdaq: INCY) today announced a clinical trial collaboration to evaluate petosemtamab, Genmab’s investigational IgG1-bispecific antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and leucine-rich repeat containing G-protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5), in combination with INCB161734, Incyte’s investigational, potent and selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, and standard-of-care chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer harboring a KRAS G12D mutation, an area with substantial unmet medical need.

“This collaboration supports our broader development strategy for petosemtamab as we explore its potential across treatment settings and in novel combinations,” said Judith Klimovsky, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Development Officer, Genmab. “Partnering with Incyte enables us to evaluate this investigational combination in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer, reflecting our commitment to research collaborations aimed at expanding potential treatment options for more patients.”

“Metastatic colorectal cancer remains difficult-to-treat, underscoring the importance of evaluating novel combinations grounded in complementary scientific approaches with the potential to enhance efficacy,” said Pablo J. Cagnoni, M.D., President, Incyte and Global Head of Research and Development. “Our collaboration with Genmab will explore the potential of combining KRAS G12D inhibition with LGR5-targeted EGFR inhibition and standard-of-care chemotherapy, with the goal of advancing a new first-line treatment approach for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer.”

Under the collaboration, Genmab will conduct the Phase 1/2 study evaluating petosemtamab in combination with INCB161734 and standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated mCRC in the first-line setting. Incyte will co-fund the study and provide clinical supply of INCB161734.

KRAS mutations occur in approximately 40% of colorectal cancers, with G12D being the most common KRAS mutation. These cancers are associated with poor prognosis, underscoring the need for new treatment approaches. The collaboration reflects a shared focus on investigating whether agents with distinct and potentially complementary mechanisms, combined with standard-of-care chemotherapy, may offer a path toward a new treatment option for patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer.

About Petosemtamab (GEN1158)

Petosemtamab is an investigational human IgG1-based bispecific antibody targeting the EGFR and the LGR5 and designed to support multiple anti-tumor mechanisms. It inhibits EGFR-mediated signaling by engaging a unique site on the receptor to prevent ligand binding. In addition, petosemtamab triggers EGFR degradation in cancer stem-like cells expressing both EGFR and LGR5. Petosemtamab is also engineered to enhance innate immune-mediated activity through interactions with macrophages and natural killer cells. It is currently being investigated in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and other solid tumors, including colorectal cancer (CRC). Petosemtamab is being evaluated in combination with chemotherapy in two Phase 3 trials in first- and second-line RAS/BRAF wild-type metastatic CRC. Please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/ for more information.

data.title: VRL Logistics to buy back 87.5 lakh shares at ₹320 per share
data.description:
VRL Logistics’ share buyback offer will open on October 27 and close on November 2, with the company proposing to repurchase up to 87.5 lakh equity shares at ₹320 apiece, according to its letter of offer filed on Saturday, October 24.

The buyback represents 5% of the company’s paid-up equity share capital as of March 31, 2026. The company will spend up to ₹280 crore on the offer, excluding transaction costs. The record date to determine eligible shareholders was October 22.

VRL Logistics said the buyback is aimed at returning surplus cash to shareholders and improving returns. “The current Buyback proposal is in line with the Company’s capital allocation practices of returning excess cash to shareholders, thereby increasing shareholder value in the longer term, and improving the Return on Equity,” it said in the letter of offer.

The promoter and promoter group have decided not to participate in the buyback.

Small shareholders have an indicative entitlement of 14 shares for every 99 shares held on the record date, while other eligible shareholders have an indicative entitlement of 19 shares for every 154 shares held. Shareholders holding up to 750 shares on the record date have been classified as small shareholders.

The offer will be carried out through the tender offer route on a proportionate basis, subject to the reservation for small shareholders. The last date for settlement of bids and payment to eligible shareholders is November 9.

VRL Logistics said the buyback will be funded from free reserves or other permitted sources, and that borrowed funds from banks and financial institutions will not be used.

data.title: A Historic Income-Tax Battle Is Playing Out at the Ballot Box — Barrons.com
data.description:
From billionaire wealth taxes to flat-rate caps, midterm voters are being pulled into an ideological tug-of-war over state policy.

By Elijah Nicholson-Messmer

A record number of state income tax fights are coming to a head this November.

Nine income tax-related measures are on the ballot nationwide, the highest number of initiatives in any year since at least the turn of the century, according to Ballotpedia data.

Those efforts range from a wealth tax on billionaires to proposals that would limit or eliminate state income taxes.

The majority of this year's measures are seeking to cut or limit state taxes.

In Washington, Initiative 645 would repeal the state's newly enacted 9.9% tax on annual individual income over $1 million, which is scheduled to take effect beginning in 2028. It would also bar state and local governments from taxing individual income or levying taxes based on it.

"I think when you see that type of movement and momentum around tax policy, especially historic and meaningful changes like we saw in Washington, it's not always going to sit well with folks," says Aidan Davis, state policy director at the Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy, a non-profit, non-partisan think tank. "And so you're going to see pushback."

That tension is clearer still in California and Colorado, where voters are being presented with diametrically opposed tax policies.

California has its dueling measures on the same ballot. Proposition 40 would impose a one-time wealth tax of up to 5% on taxpayers and trusts with covered assets valued over $1 billion. Proposition 42 would nullify the wealth tax by prohibiting new state taxes on personal property. Polling puts both measures at roughly equal odds of success. In the event that both measures pass, the one that receives the higher number of votes will take effect.

A third measure — Proposition 3 — would make permanent California's current top marginal tax rates, which range from 10.3% to 12.3% and apply to personal income over $360,000 for single filers, $490,000 for heads of household, and $721,000 for joint filers. Revenue from these taxes are used to support schools and community colleges. On Kalshi, Prop 3 currently has the highest odds of passage of any income tax-related ballot measure this year.

For Colorado voters, the potential results of two opposing measures is less clear. Amendment 87 would replace the state's flat tax, enacted in 1987, with graduated rates ranging from 3.71% in the lowest bracket to 8.41% in the highest. Proposition 136 — a direct counter to Amendment 87 — would cap individual and corporate income tax rates at the current rate of 4.4%.

Opponents of Amendment 87 argue that graduated taxes would put Colorado's small businesses at a "competitive disadvantage" against out-of-state rivals.

"The result would be some combination of reduced investment and growth, business attrition, lower wages, and higher prices," Jared Walczak, senior fellow at the Tax Foundation, a non-profit, non-partisan think tank, wrote in a recent note.

There is no current polling on the two measures, but Kalshi markets suggest the graduated tax amendment has a much lower chance of passing than the proposition that would nullify it.

Still, should both measures pass, experts say it isn't clear which could ultimately take effect. Because one measure is a constitutional amendment and one is a statute, the simple rule that applies in California's case doesn't extend to Colorado.

"It's a little unclear at this time what will happen in Colorado if both are approved, even if the cap gets more votes," says Ryan Byrne, ballots team managing editor at Ballotpedia. "These things are often litigated. If both are approved, we'll undoubtedly have litigation."

Measures in North Carolina and Iowa have a clearer path forward. In North Carolina, a constitutional amendment would change the state's income tax rate cap from 7% to 3.5%. The amendment is estimated to have no fiscal impact as the applicable taxes already have rates under the proposed 3.5% cap. No polling is available on the amendment, but a Kalshi market puts its chance of approval at roughly 80%.

In Iowa, Amendment 1 would require a two-thirds majority in each chamber of the General Assembly to pass any bill enacting or increasing individual, corporate or certain other taxes. Average support for the amendment is about 64%, but polling results vary by more than 40 percentage points.

Historically, voters have shown roughly equivalent support for ballot measures that cut or limit taxes as those that raise them, Ballotpedia data shows. But, as Missouri voters have shown, there are exceptions to that rule.

Missouri voters broadly rejected Amendment 5 in August, a ballot measure that sought to reduce — and eventually eliminate — the state individual income tax based on revenue growth. Less than 17% of Missourians voted for the amendment.

To offset lost income tax revenue, the amendment would have allowed lawmakers to expand sales taxes to currently untaxed goods and services and raise the state's existing sales tax rate.

The amendment would have led to an average net tax increase for 80% of the state's residents, with only the wealthiest Missourians seeing a tax cut, according to the Missouri Budget Project, a non-profit, non-partisan think tank.

The clarity with which voters can see those trade-offs has major implications for the success of a ballot measure, Davis says.

"We've seen a lot of cuts over the past five, 10 years in states on their income taxes. A lot of the time, those tax cuts were happening without any conversation about what the trade-offs look like when you cut income taxes," Davis says. "I think the difference in what happened in Missouri is that that trade-off conversation was right front and center in front of the voters."

Exactly how those trade-offs resonate with voters in other states will become clear this November.

data.title: Genmab and Incyte Announce Clinical Trial Collaboration in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer
data.description:
Genmab A/S () and Incyte () today announced a clinical trial collaboration to evaluate petosemtamab, Genmab’s investigational IgG1-bispecific antibody targeting the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) and leucine-rich repeat containing G-protein-coupled receptor 5 (LGR5), in combination with INCB161734, Incyte’s investigational, potent and selective KRAS G12D inhibitor, and standard-of-care chemotherapy as a first-line treatment for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer harboring a KRAS G12D mutation, an area with substantial unmet medical need.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261024542855/en/

“This collaboration supports our broader development strategy for petosemtamab as we explore its potential across treatment settings and in novel combinations,” said Judith Klimovsky, M.D., Executive Vice President and Chief Development Officer, Genmab. “Partnering with Incyte enables us to evaluate this investigational combination in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer, reflecting our commitment to research collaborations aimed at expanding potential treatment options for more patients.”

“Metastatic colorectal cancer remains difficult-to-treat, underscoring the importance of evaluating novel combinations grounded in complementary scientific approaches with the potential to enhance efficacy,” said Pablo J. Cagnoni, M.D., President, Incyte and Global Head of Research and Development. “Our collaboration with Genmab will explore the potential of combining KRAS G12D inhibition with LGR5-targeted EGFR inhibition and standard-of-care chemotherapy, with the goal of advancing a new first-line treatment approach for patients with metastatic colorectal cancer.”

Under the collaboration, Genmab will conduct the Phase 1/2 study evaluating petosemtamab in combination with INCB161734 and standard-of-care chemotherapy in patients with KRAS G12D-mutated mCRC in the first-line setting. Incyte will co-fund the study and provide clinical supply of INCB161734.

KRAS mutations occur in approximately 40% of colorectal cancers, with G12D being the most common KRAS mutation. These cancers are associated with poor prognosis, underscoring the need for new treatment approaches. The collaboration reflects a shared focus on investigating whether agents with distinct and potentially complementary mechanisms, combined with standard-of-care chemotherapy, may offer a path toward a new treatment option for patients with KRAS G12D-mutated metastatic colorectal cancer.

About Petosemtamab (GEN1158)
Petosemtamab is an investigational human IgG1-based bispecific antibody targeting the EGFR and the LGR5 and designed to support multiple anti-tumor mechanisms. It inhibits EGFR-mediated signaling by engaging a unique site on the receptor to prevent ligand binding. In addition, petosemtamab triggers EGFR degradation in cancer stem-like cells expressing both EGFR and LGR5. Petosemtamab is also engineered to enhance innate immune-mediated activity through interactions with macrophages and natural killer cells. It is currently being investigated in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and other solid tumors, including colorectal cancer (CRC). Petosemtamab is being evaluated in combination with chemotherapy in two Phase 3 trials in first- and second-line RAS/BRAF wild-type metastatic CRC. Please visit https://clinicaltrials.gov/ for more information.

About INCB161734
INCB161734 is an investigational, novel, selective and orally bioavailable small molecule ON/OFF KRAS G12D inhibitor. KRAS is one of the most frequently altered oncogenic drivers across solid tumors, and the KRAS G12D mutation is among the most common KRAS alterations, occurring in approximately 40% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) cases and approximately 15% of colorectal cancer (CRC) cases.

INCB161734 is being evaluated in the global Phase 3 DAWN-303 (NCT07522073) study which is currently enrolling patients with previously untreated KRAS G12D-mutated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of INCB161734 in combination with standard-of-care (SoC) chemotherapy.

INCB161734 is also being evaluated as a monotherapy and in combination with standard-of-care (SoC) chemotherapy (gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel [GEMNabP] or modified FOLFIRINOX [mFOLFIRINOX]), in an ongoing open-label Phase 1 study across KRAS G12D-mutated solid tumors (NCT06179160).

About Genmab
Genmab is an international biotechnology company dedicated to improving the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases through innovative antibody medicines. For over 25 years, its passionate, innovative and collaborative team has advanced a broad range of antibody-based therapeutic formats, including bispecific antibodies, antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs), immune-modulating antibodies and other next-generation modalities. Genmab’s science powers eight approved antibody medicines, and the company is advancing a strong late-stage clinical pipeline, including wholly owned programs, with the goal of delivering transformative medicines to patients.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com or follow us on LinkedIn, X, Facebook and Instagram.

Incyte is redefining what’s possible in biopharmaceutical innovation. Through deep scientific expertise and a relentless focus on patients, we have built an established portfolio of first-in-class medicines and an extensive portfolio of next-generation medicines across our key franchises: Hematology, Oncology and Inflammation & Autoimmunity.

data.title: Better logistics, trade pacts, policy support can boost India's rice exports: Industry leaders at BIRC 2026
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Better port infrastructure, greater utilisation of free trade agreements (FTAs) and supportive government policies can help India strengthen its position in global rice markets, industry leaders said at the Bharat International Rice Conference (BIRC) 2026 on Saturday.

During a panel discussion on trade policies, export incentives and market opportunities, experts emphasised improving logistics, expanding access to international markets and aligning rice production with global demand.

Ravi Gupta, Executive Director and Board Member, Shree Renuka Sugars Limited, highlighted the importance of efficient transportation and shipping infrastructure for agricultural exports.

"Are we equipped enough for the logistics?" Gupta asked, stressing that competitiveness depends not only on rice quality and pricing but also on timely delivery to international buyers.

He called for better utilisation of ports in Odisha and West Bengal, including Haldia, and a comprehensive policy to facilitate agricultural cargo shipments.

Tarun Bajaj, former Director, SEBI, and Senior Consultant, APLOA, highlighted the benefits of FTAs in reducing tariffs, addressing trade barriers and making export procedures more predictable.

"FTA has definitely given us a bonus," Bajaj said, adding that exporters should take advantage of government support schemes.

He also indicated that APEDA's export promotion scheme was expected to become operational within days.

Shubhranshu Mishra, Additional Secretary, Government of Odisha, and Managing Director, APICOL, outlined the state's ambition to increase rice exports from around Rs 321 crore to Rs 10,000 crore by 2047.

"Our export strategy cannot be a residual approach," Mishra said, emphasising the need to identify international demand and develop production and aggregation systems accordingly.

Prashant Raizada, Trade Compliance and Incentives, EY, highlighted opportunities in markets including the UK, Australia, Switzerland and Norway.

He noted that the UK and Australia account for only around 1.26 per cent and 0.38 per cent, respectively, of India's total rice exports, indicating significant scope for market expansion.

"So, we have data to prove that these free trade agreements are definitely helping the country," Raizada said, urging exporters to leverage existing trade agreements.

Rajesh Paharia, Chief Manager, Business Development, KRIBHCO Agri, highlighted the importance of a stable export policy environment, noting that India's rice trade had faced relatively few policy disruptions during 2025-26.

He also pointed to changing import regulations in African markets, including Senegal and Kenya, which exporters need to navigate.

Rajiv Kumar, Executive Director, The Rice Exporters Association (TREA), highlighted opportunities through international trade finance and humanitarian procurement programmes.

He also stressed the importance of addressing pesticide-residue compliance requirements to improve market access and reduce shipment rejections.

The conference also witnessed the launch of "The Rice Economy: India, the World and the Future of Rice", authored by Dr Prem Garg, examining India's rice sector and its future in global trade.

The Bharat International Rice Conference 2026 is being held from October 23 to 25 in New Delhi, bringing together Indian exporters, international buyers and other stakeholders in the global rice trade.

data.title: PM Modi to visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on October 25
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on Sunday (October 25), where he will inaugurate a garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, witness the Indian Air Force's aerial display at Namo Ghat and inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, according to a press release.

At around 11 am, the Prime Minister will inaugurate Arvind Limited's new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, followed by the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat at around 1 pm, where he will attend as the chief guest.

The garment manufacturing facility is expected to strengthen India's textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem and promote industrial growth in the region, the release stated.

Focusing on modern manufacturing practices, the facility will create employment opportunities, particularly for women, and contribute to the region's economic progress. With a global customer base, it will also enable products manufactured in Varanasi to reach international markets, the release added.

The inauguration is expected to highlight Uttar Pradesh's growing role as a destination for industrial investment and manufacturing-led growth, while the predominantly women-led initiative reflects the focus on women-led development.

The Prime Minister will thereafter witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat, organised to commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force under the theme "Wings over Ganges".

The aerial display will feature aircraft, including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, SU-30MKI and Rafale, along with transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, showcasing jointness in operations.

The Indian Air Force's premier display teams, including the Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and the Sarang Helicopter Display Team, will participate in the event, demonstrating precision flying, coordination and operational excellence, according to the release.

Thereafter, Modi will travel to Odisha, where he will inaugurate the RBI's Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar at around 4.45 pm and address the gathering.

The newly established facilities are aimed at strengthening the technological foundations of India's financial system by providing a secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing ecosystem for the RBI and the broader financial sector, the release stated.

Four state-of-the-art data centres will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other flagship initiatives. The facility has been certified to the Uptime Institute Tier IV standard, a global benchmark for data centre infrastructure, placing it in the highest tier of operational resilience.

According to the release, the facility is among the largest Tier IV-certified facilities in the Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI) sector worldwide.

It is expected to improve the reach, efficiency and reliability of digital financial services and provide a secure digital foundation for India's increasingly technology-driven financial economy. It will also strengthen the RBI's position in digital infrastructure among central banks.

The Cybersecurity Training Institute will provide a dedicated platform for cybersecurity and enterprise-technology training, research and capability development across the sector.

The institute will focus on cutting-edge technologies relevant to the BFSI sector, including quantum computing, artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies, the release added.

data.title: Karnataka CM D K Shivakumar grants prosecution sanction against IAS officer Gyanendra Gangwar in KPSC recruitment scam
data.description:
Bengaluru, Oct. 24 -- Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar on Saturday issued prosecution sanction against IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in the case related to corruption and large-scale irregularities in the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) recruitment examination.

In a post on X, Shivakumar said the government had taken a serious view of corruption affecting the credibility of the public recruitment system and reiterated its commitment to transparency and integrity in governance.

He said, "No Room for Corruption, No Protection for the Guilty. Permission has been granted to prosecute IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar in a corruption case related to the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) recruitment scam. Our government will not tolerate any actions that toy with the future of the youth."

Emphasising the government's stand on corruption and accountability in administration, Shivakumar said there would be no leniency for actions that undermine public trust in the recruitment process.

"The government has taken a serious view of corruption that undermines the credibility of the public recruitment system. Prioritizing transparency and integrity in governance is our commitment. There is no room for corruption in our government, and no leniency for actions that cast a shadow on administration," he added.

The sanction paves the way for the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and Enforcement Directorate (ED) to file a chargesheet and prosecute the suspended officer under the Prevention of Corruption Act and other relevant provisions.

Gangwar, a 2016-batch IAS officer of Karnataka cadre, was serving as Controller of Examinations at KPSC between January 2024 and March 2026.

He was arrested on August 29 this year for allegedly leaking question papers of the KPSC Veterinary Officer recruitment exam.

According to the CID investigation, Gangwar allegedly leaked the question papers of the competitive examination held on January 8 and 9, 2026, for 400 posts of Veterinary Officers, to at least 10 candidates who eventually figured in the top 20 rank list. The final list was announced on July 17, 2026.

The agency found that aspirants were charged between Rs. 20 lakh and Rs. 80 lakh per paper. The money was allegedly collected through middleman Basavaraj Kannale, who was arrested on August 30.

Kannale allegedly collected money through Om Lakshmi Souharda Co-operative Society, Bidar, and used it to purchase gold jewellery worth Rs. 54 lakh, pay Rs. 11 lakh for air tickets for Gangwar, and arrange logistics for candidates.

Investigators alleged that selected candidates were taken to a resort on the outskirts of Bengaluru, provided with the leaked question paper and made to memorise answers under Kannale's supervision. On the exam day, they were transported to centres in vehicles arranged by the accused.

Both Gangwar and Kannale have been booked under Section 318(3) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for cheating and breach of trust and Section 10 of the Karnataka Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Corruption and Unfair Means of Recruitment) Act, 2023. The ED is also probing money laundering charges.

The CID had approached the state government for sanction under Section 218 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, which mandates government sanction to prosecute state officers.

A Bengaluru court had earlier rejected Gangwar's bail plea, noting prima facie material showing a money trail and risk of evidence tampering, including destruction of a Xiaomi tablet used in the offence.

The government had also indicated it is exploring legal options to shut down KPSC itself following widespread irregularities, with CM Shivakumar stating that the chairman and other officials are under the scanner.

The CID is due to file its chargesheet by November 26, within 90 days of the first arrest.

data.title: India On The Right Path To Build Its Own Aircraft Engine, Says Rossell Techsys CEO
data.description:
CEO Senthil Balasubramanian discusses India’s aerospace and defence growth, supply-chain resilience, semiconductors, aircraft engines and MRO

In an interview with BW Businessworld, Senthil Balasubramanian, CEO of Rossell Techsys, spoke about the company’s growth plans and the changing aerospace and defence landscape. He discussed supply-chain resilience, India’s push for self-reliance, semiconductor opportunities, indigenous aircraft engine development, and Rossell Techsys’ expansion into space and MRO. Excerpts:

The aerospace and defence sector is booming, and the government is also strongly supporting it. How critical do you think government support will be for the sector’s growth?

There is a lot happening globally in aerospace and defence. There are conflicts in several parts of the world, and governments have realised that they need to build greater resilience and strengthen their defence capabilities. In India too, following Operation Sindoor, defence spending has received greater attention.

I believe this trend will continue for several years, with major countries increasing their defence expenditure. We are fortunate to be present across several defence platforms. We work with customers such as Boeing and Lockheed Martin and have also received supplier recognition from both companies.

Rossell Techsys has been in this business for 15 years, so we are well positioned to benefit from this global trend.

The other important aspect is the ecosystem. I participate in several industry forums, and one issue that frequently comes up is how MSMEs can collaborate and support each other. Supply-chain resilience remains a challenge for India. We have skilled manpower, but to build a successful manufacturing ecosystem, we need a strong and resilient supply chain.

Government schemes and incentives can play an important role in developing that ecosystem and supporting companies as they scale.

You mentioned supply-chain resilience. There is a broader concern about dependence on China. How do you see this issue from the perspective of aerospace and defence?

In defence programmes, we do not source parts from China, so we have zero dependency on China's supply chain. Around 80 per cent of our supply base today is from the US.

Defence contracts are highly controlled from a documentation and sourcing perspective. They specify which parts and suppliers can be used, and companies cannot simply deviate from those requirements.

The remaining 20 per cent of our supply base largely consists of packaging, consumables and similar items. So, in defence, there is effectively no dependence on China.

We are also beginning to see similar trends in other industries, including semiconductors and space. It is not yet 100 per cent implemented, but there is increasing caution around sourcing components from China for security reasons.

A large part of your business is linked to the US. Given the changes and uncertainty in US policy under President Donald Trump, do you see any concerns?

Fortunately, our products are linked to defence platforms and ultimately to companies such as Boeing, which is a major supplier to the US government. Our exports to the US currently face zero tariffs.

Around 90-95 per cent of our sales are exports, of which approximately 80 per cent goes to the US. Around 15 per cent goes to markets such as Israel and Malaysia, while about 5 per cent is in India.

So, at present, we have not seen an impact from tariffs. These are defence-related products that are required by the US, and the country continues to have significant defence requirements globally. That gives us confidence regarding our US business.

Do you see Rossell Techsys diversifying its markets beyond the US, particularly into Europe and Africa?

Rossell Techsys is doing very well in the US, but we are not yet significantly present in Europe. We are, however, in discussions with several major European players and have received three or four requests for information from large European customers.

I have to be careful about naming them because we do not have signed contracts yet. But there is significant interest from European companies.

Europe has strong technology capabilities, but scalability can be a challenge because of manpower constraints. India can play an important role as a partner because of its talent pool and engineering capabilities.

One of India's longstanding challenges in aerospace and defence is engine technology. Given your experience in the sector, do you think India can develop and manufacture its own aircraft engines in the future?

Engine technology is extremely complex. Companies such as GE and Pratt & Whitney have spent decades developing aircraft engines, and there are only a handful of companies globally with this capability.

India can certainly develop its own engine technology, but it will take time. The country is moving in the right direction. India is no longer known only for its labour force; it is increasingly recognised for technology, engineering and design capabilities.

As I mentioned earlier, supply-chain resilience is also important. India is on the right path, and eventually I believe the country will have its own fully designed and manufactured aircraft engine.

You mentioned the semiconductor business. Given concerns over raw materials and China's control over several parts of the supply chain, what challenges could the Indian semiconductor industry face?

Unlike defence, semiconductor companies currently do source certain parts from China. However, there is a significant push from the Indian government towards greater self-reliance and building a domestic manufacturing ecosystem.

That ecosystem will take time to develop. India is moving in the right direction, but there is still some dependence on China today.

The government is also providing incentives for companies to invest in semiconductors and develop domestic manufacturing and engineering capabilities. India cannot simply become a manufacturing destination. We also need to develop our own technologies, components and eventually raw-material capabilities.

Over time, these dependencies on China should reduce, but we are not there yet.

Many industry leaders argue that India needs to move beyond manufacturing-linked incentives towards design-linked incentives. What is your view?

The government has recently announced incentives for semiconductors, which will help local companies and MSMEs invest in the sector. That is a good start.

But there needs to be much more focus on technology, engineering capabilities, design and training.

At Rossell, we have our own school of learning where we train employees. That is a significant advantage for us. When space and semiconductor companies engage with us, they are comfortable because we have the internal capabilities to execute programmes without depending heavily on external support.

Training is a major part of building the ecosystem. Retaining employees is equally important. It is not simply about attracting talent; companies need to attract, train and retain talent. All three are critical for the success of the semiconductor, space and defence industries.

What further reforms or measures do you think the government should undertake to strengthen India's semiconductor sector, particularly chip manufacturing and design?

The government has already made several announcements, and there will likely be more. We are seeing major US companies announcing investments in India, while more companies are looking at India for semiconductor design, manufacturing and services.

There are two major drivers of semiconductor demand today: data centres and artificial intelligence. Both are driving demand at an unprecedented pace.

Several large companies describe the current expansion as a massive ramp-up, and they expect this growth to continue for at least the next three years. Beyond that, it is difficult to predict how the market will evolve.

What is your view of India's efforts to create dedicated zones and ecosystems for aerospace manufacturing and exports?

Rossell operates in an EOU, or Export Oriented Unit, area and is located next to Boeing. An EOU is different from a Special Economic Zone and comes with its own set of privileges.

We recently also received a DTA, or Domestic Tariff Area, licence. This allows us to work with Indian companies such as HAL and Tata. Previously, there were restrictions associated with our EOU status when it came to domestic business.

With the DTA licence, we can now bid for business with Indian customers. So, we are not in an SEZ; we operate under the EOU framework and now also have the required DTA approval.

Your order pipeline includes significant orders. What products and equipment will you supply under these orders?

Our orders and pipeline are predominantly across three areas. First, we are primarily a wire-harness company. We have been designing, manufacturing and servicing wire harnesses for 15 years. Second, we are developing automatic test equipment, or ATEs. We integrate these into complete solutions for Indian companies and are also engaging with US and European companies. Third, we have entered fibre optics, which is a new technology area for Rossell. We have invested in this capability and are engaging with both Indian and international companies.

The order values you mentioned will predominantly be across these three areas: wire harnesses, automatic test equipment and fibre optics.

We are also entering the MRO, or maintenance, repair and overhaul, business. We recently received the required certification and are now pursuing orders in this area.

For the past 15 years, Rossell has primarily focused on design and manufacturing. We are now expanding into the aftermarket, which represents a significant opportunity.

You are expanding your aerospace manufacturing footprint in Bengaluru. What will the new facility add to your operations?

Rossell currently operates from a 225,000-square-foot facility in Bengaluru's Aerospace Defence Park and has around 1,500 employees here.

All three of our verticals, defence, space and semiconductors, are growing strongly. We have therefore decided to lease another 210,000-square-foot building in the same industrial park, about three minutes from our existing facility.

The new facility will support our future expansion. It is expected to be ready in the next three to four weeks. Once operational, we will have 225,000 square feet at our existing location and another 210,000 square feet at the new facility.

Your recent financial results showed 138 per cent year-on-year growth in PBT and 78 per cent growth in revenue. What drove this significant growth?

The results you are referring to are for Q1. We reported 138 per cent growth in PBT and 78 per cent growth in revenue.

Rossell started working with Boeing 12-15 years ago with one platform. Today, we are qualified across multiple Boeing platforms. We have also diversified into space and semiconductor businesses, which have provided a significant boost to our revenue.

Today, we have three major verticals. Aerospace and defence will always remain our core business. The second is space programmes, and the third is semiconductors.

In space, we are qualified to manufacture wire harnesses for satellite programmes. Last year, we delivered certain volumes, and this year the customer has asked us to triple those volumes. That is contributing to both revenue and profitability.

In semiconductors, we have been qualified by a major US-based company, which has qualified several parts with us. We are growing significantly with that customer and see substantial opportunities in both space and semiconductors going forward.

These factors explain the significant jump in our revenue and profitability.

What are your expectations for Q2 results, given the order pipeline and growth opportunities?

I have to be careful about making forward-looking financial statements. But I can say that Rossell will continue to deliver strong financial results.

If you look at our cumulative performance over the last 13-14 years, we believe we can deliver a comparable level of business in the next two financial years. That indicates the pace at which we are growing.

We expect this momentum to continue through Q2, Q3 and Q4.

So, are you confident about the Q2 performance and the quarters that follow?

Yes. We expect good results in Q2, followed by Q3 and Q4. We are well positioned to deliver strong growth.

Looking ahead, how do you see Rossell Techsys developing over the next five to 10 years?

This is again a forward-looking statement, but we have clear visibility across our businesses. Whether it is aerospace and defence, semiconductors or space programmes, we see significant opportunities.

We are also expanding into MRO and have a US location that is attracting considerable attention. We recently passed an audit in the US and are beginning to manufacture certain wire harnesses there. Some of these are ITAR-controlled products and therefore need to be manufactured in the US.

With the US facility ramping up and our business units in India continuing to grow, we expect our sales to increase significantly over the next three to five years.
